text:
mira: Heads-up — during the int4 bring-up for model-neo-13B-long we started seeing progressive context drift when the prefill is staggered across micro-batches. Repro steps below, minimal logs attached.

noah: Can you paste the exact repro command + seed? also are you using deterministic batching?

mira: repro:```bash
python run_infer.py \
  --model model-neo-13B-long \
  --quant int4 \
  --prefill-mode staggered \
  --micro-batch 2 \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --seq-len 4096 \
  --seed 42
```
Observed: around token ~1500 we get repeated token sequences and semantics drift vs float32 baseline. quick log snippet:```
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] kvcache[shard-0] append idx=4092 -> stored_pos=8
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] WARNING: rope_scale_mismatch layer=8 expected_scale=1.0 got=0.996
[2026-03-18T10:12:34Z] generated: "The cat sat on the ... the cat sat on the ..."
```

rachel: Hmm, we had a rotary scaling tweak last week (PR #3421) that changed per-layer scale interpolation for micro-batch fusion. Might interact badly with quantized KV index math. Can you run with the old kernel flag?

arun: Quick hypothesis: staggered prefill leaves overlapping KV write windows that are compacted differently in int4 pack layout, causing index wrap or shadowing. Try: contiguous-prefill (single micro-batch) and also set PREFILL_COALESCE=0 to force explicit writes.

mira: good call. Running contiguous now, will post diffs.

jessica: Also capture the kvcache dump (first/last pos per shard) + token map. In past bugs we saw "stored_pos" jump backwards when micro-batch reorder happened during memcpy optimizations. If you can share the dump I'll do a quick scan.

mira: attaching kvcache-dump snippet (trimmed):```
SHARD 0: first=0 last=4092 capacity=8192
SHARD 1: first=4093 last=8185 capacity=8192
MAPPING: token_range[1400-1600] -> shard0@{offsets:4080..4100}
```

noah: If contiguous run removes the drift then this points to a write-serialization bug in the int4 pack path. If it still reproduces, maybe quantized kernel does per-token rotary scaling with cumulative FP error.

mira: contiguous run: no drift after same length, generation matches float32 baseline diff < 0.2 BLEU-ish. so micro-batch ordering is suspect.

rachel: OK that narrows it. I'll bisect the rotary interpolation change and the micro-batch coalescing kernel. can someone add a small unit that simulates staggered writes to the int4 pack writer? would help repro in CI.

jessica: I'll add a tiny fuzz test: staggered-prefill-smoke that reproduces the index shadowing in ~1k runs, and post a link.

ci-bot: CI: https://ci.internal.redwood/eng-ml/3421-staggered-prefill-smoke — failing on int4-pack-writes on x86-gpu-2 (run #27) :x:

mira: thanks — putting a short PR with a mitigation (serialize prefill writes) to test. will follow up once CI runs. :thumbsup:

noah: if we have a mitigation, also run perf delta. serializing could increase tail latency. consider a fast-path that detects contiguous micro-batches and keeps fused writes.

mira: noted. I'll capture perf numbers in the PR.

arun: great triage, folks. keep the shortnotes in the bug ticket so we can roll into release notes if needed. :spiral_calendar:

mira: will do, closing thread for now — will ping when PR lands and CI green.
